items.title: Use the current tutorial location and record the version
items.source_observation: The old Scanpy tutorial repository is archived and points to tutorial sources in the main repository. scvi-tutorials separately hosts scvi-tools notebook sources.
items.proposed_rule: Log the tutorial URL, access date, installed package versions and a commit or release when available. Check whether an example is current or explicitly legacy before adapting it.
items.applicability_and_limits: Repository location is provenance, not a scientific quality score. A directory listing does not establish that all notebooks have been evaluated.
items.plugin_relationship: Documentation improvement only; existing analysis commands are unchanged.
items.review_question: Which tutorials should we maintain as supported examples, and which should remain historical reading?
items.proposed_acceptance_check: A proposed workflow cites its specific source and environment rather than claiming compatibility from the repository name.

items.title: Inspect QC per sample and revisit exclusions
items.source_observation: The Scanpy tutorial recommends inspecting sample-specific QC distributions and revisiting permissive initial filtering after examining the data structure.
items.proposed_rule: Before adopting a cutoff, record the sample-level distribution and the affected populations. Compare a small, justified alternative and retain both exclusion ledgers.
items.applicability_and_limits: Applies to cell filtering. A permissive first pass is exploratory and does not mean every retained cell is suitable for final inference.
items.plugin_relationship: Existing inspect-only mode, per-sample filters and ledgers support this review. Population-aware sensitivity reporting is still manual.
items.review_question: Which tissue-specific evidence would make you retain a low-complexity population or remove it?
items.proposed_acceptance_check: Compare retained cells by sample and candidate population under two predeclared settings; explain losses, not only the final UMAP.

items.title: Do not transfer a MAD multiplier without its definition
items.source_observation: The QC chapter applies MAD rules to transformed QC metrics. Its example is not numerically identical to our raw-metric suggestion implementation.
items.proposed_rule: Record the metric transformation, MAD scaling convention, multiplier and whether the result is merely suggested or applied.
items.applicability_and_limits: Robust outlier rules still need tissue and sample context. Equal multipliers do not imply equal thresholds when conventions differ.
items.plugin_relationship: Our suggestions use median plus/minus 3 times 1.4826 times MAD on recorded metrics and are not automatically applied. Do not silently replace them with the chapter recipe.
items.review_question: Should we compare raw and log-scale QC suggestions for each tissue, and how would you decide between them?
items.proposed_acceptance_check: On a fixed QC vector, explicitly compute both definitions and compare which cells change status.

items.title: Define the physical capture before detecting doublets
items.source_observation: The tutorials run doublet detection with sample/batch separation rather than treating independent captures as one mixture.
items.proposed_rule: Resolve capture IDs before detection. Inspect scores alongside competing markers and cell quality, and record the expected-rate assumption.
items.applicability_and_limits: Capture, donor and condition are not automatically interchangeable. A doublet call and ambient RNA contamination require different investigations.
items.plugin_relationship: Current optional Scrublet runs by capture and requires sufficient eligible cells; scDblFinder is not implemented.
items.review_question: How are captures, pooled donors and multiplexing recorded in your experiments?
items.proposed_acceptance_check: A dataset with two captures is processed with the correct grouping; cells with conflicting markers receive an evidence review rather than automatic identity claims.

items.title: Treat ambient RNA correction as a separate, auditable branch
items.source_observation: SoupX documents a channel-level workflow with droplet and cell-count inputs, clustering information, contamination estimation and adjusted counts.
items.proposed_rule: First establish suitable source matrices and contamination evidence. If tested, save corrected counts separately and compare selected markers and downstream conclusions with the uncorrected branch.
items.applicability_and_limits: This is a candidate extension, not a requirement for every dataset. A filtered matrix alone may not provide the demonstrated input context.
items.plugin_relationship: SoupX is not installed as a plugin tool. No correction or matrix replacement is authorized by this note.
items.review_question: Which marker patterns and negative controls would convince you that apparent expression is contamination?
items.proposed_acceptance_check: Predeclare diagnostic genes and evaluate correction magnitude and biological signal preservation, retaining both matrices and method versions.

items.title: Validate every component before combining matrices
items.source_observation: A forum reporter inspected early rows, missed a normalized dataset later in a concatenated object, and subsequently identified that mixed representation as the cause of count warnings.
items.proposed_rule: Validate each source dataset before concatenation and inspect all stored nonzero values in bounded chunks, alongside processing provenance. Do not round transformed values into counts.
items.applicability_and_limits: This is a firsthand debugging case, not evidence that every fractional matrix has the same origin. Some assays or quantifiers produce fractional values legitimately.
items.plugin_relationship: Existing numeric count checks help reject incompatible values; future multi-matrix intake needs per-source provenance. Multi-matrix assembly is outside the current runner.
items.review_question: Which processing records should be mandatory when a collaborator supplies a merged H5AD?
items.proposed_acceptance_check: A fixture with a normalized block at the end fails intake even though its initial rows appear count-like.

items.title: A raw slot is not a verified raw-count archive
items.source_observation: The AnnData excerpt initializes raw with a copy; a historical issue reports unexpected mutation after assignment. The scvi-tools tutorial also uses raw for normalized values.
items.proposed_rule: Document representation explicitly, preserve a separate counts copy and verify that later transformations do not modify it. Do not infer numeric meaning from the attribute name.
items.applicability_and_limits: The historical issue is not reproduced here. The AnnData page was only available as an indexed official excerpt; review current-version behavior before accepting a precise copy contract.
items.plugin_relationship: The plugin uses a named counts layer and independently retained input files rather than relying on raw as proof of provenance.
items.review_question: What representation names and checks should every imported H5AD provide?
items.proposed_acceptance_check: Hash the source file and compare retained counts before and after normalization/representation fitting; inspect any raw attribute independently.

items.title: Select the HVG input layer to match the method
items.source_observation: The official indexed API distinguishes logarithmized inputs from count-based seurat_v3 flavors. A technical forum reply explains explicit layer selection when normalization has already occurred in X.
items.proposed_rule: Validate the representation of the selected layer and record flavor, batch key and feature set. Changing method names without changing the input contract is not a valid comparison.
items.applicability_and_limits: The current API page was only available as an indexed excerpt. A 2023 cross-tool comparison does not prove equality across present versions or batch-ranking options.
items.plugin_relationship: The runner already uses the counts layer for seurat_v3 and log-normalized X for its seurat option.
items.review_question: Which biological signals should remain represented when alternative HVG choices are compared?
items.proposed_acceptance_check: A deliberately log-normalized counts layer is rejected; two valid HVG strategies are compared with feature overlap and downstream stability, not only runtime.

items.title: Record the normalization target instead of saying only normalized
items.source_observation: The normalize_total API documents that target_sum=None uses the median original cell total.
items.proposed_rule: Record the target, transformation and gene universe used in its denominator. Inspect downstream tool contracts before reusing the matrix.
items.applicability_and_limits: Median scaling and CP10k need not yield the same transformed numbers. Neither is automatically better for every downstream task.
items.plugin_relationship: Our plugin explicitly uses CP10k followed by log1p. This differs from a tutorial call that leaves target_sum unspecified.
items.review_question: Should all project outputs carry a machine-readable representation label including the normalization target?
items.proposed_acceptance_check: For a small fixed count matrix, recover the chosen normalized totals before log1p and verify that later tools consume the intended layer.

items.title: Check the classifier input and reference before trusting labels
items.source_observation: CellTypist documents log1p CP10k AnnData input and recommends retaining broad gene coverage for overlap with its trained model.
items.proposed_rule: If adding a classifier, record model identity, training scope and gene overlap; compare proposals with marker evidence and retain an unresolved option.
items.applicability_and_limits: This contract belongs to CellTypist, not every annotation method. Correct input formatting does not establish tissue or disease-state validity.
items.plugin_relationship: Current annotation is marker-based and reviewed; CellTypist is a possible separate tool, not an existing backend.
items.review_question: Which tissues or novel states would require rejecting or broadening an automated reference label?
items.proposed_acceptance_check: Test known reference-compatible cells alongside an intentionally out-of-scope population and review both, without forcing every prediction into a final label.

items.title: Register counts and batch deliberately for scVI
items.source_observation: The scvi-tools preparation tutorial preserves counts and explicitly registers the count layer and batch key for SCVI.
items.proposed_rule: Validate what each covariate represents before fitting. Keep an uncorrected comparison and assess both unwanted variation and biological signal retention.
items.applicability_and_limits: Only the relevant preparation sections and repository overview were inspected; this is not a completed integration benchmark. Batch correction cannot establish causality.
items.plugin_relationship: Existing scVI setup registers counts and batch; PCA remains an uncorrected baseline. Our runner does not expose every covariate option in scvi-tools.
items.review_question: When disease and processing batch overlap, what evidence would you require before interpreting a corrected representation?
items.proposed_acceptance_check: Record sample-design tables and examine donor, condition and marker patterns in both representations; flag non-identifiable comparisons.

items.title: Do not turn one donor into many biological replicates
items.source_observation: The forum thread asks how to test two conditions with one replicate each and contains no visible answer. The primary paper excerpt examines biological-replicate aggregation and pseudo-replicates.
items.proposed_rule: Check independent donors before population-level condition inference. With inadequate replication, present a restricted descriptive comparison and a request for suitable samples.
items.applicability_and_limits: The unanswered question is not a validated workaround. The paper was available only through its indexed original-article excerpt in this pass; full Methods review remains outstanding.
items.plugin_relationship: Existing DE enforces donor gates. Those software floors do not guarantee power or remove confounding.
items.review_question: What limited result would still help a researcher when replication is insufficient?
items.proposed_acceptance_check: Randomly splitting a donor into cell subsets must not satisfy the donor gate; the report must identify the true experimental unit.

items.title: Separate marker ranking from replicated condition DE
items.source_observation: The rank_genes_groups API expects logarithmized data and warns about non-independent cells in inferential comparisons.
items.proposed_rule: Label exploratory cluster-marker ranking separately from donor-level condition testing. Explicitly identify the matrix, grouping, reference and experimental unit.
items.applicability_and_limits: A marker-ranking function can be useful without providing a valid population-level condition test. Raw-count expectations depend on the method, not the word DE.
items.plugin_relationship: The plugin uses exploratory marker evidence for annotation and a separate raw-count pseudobulk path for condition DE.
items.review_question: What wording should distinguish a candidate marker from a replicated disease-associated gene in reports?
items.proposed_acceptance_check: A report must not present cell-level marker p-values as donor-replicated evidence; trace every contrast to its design and representation.

items.title: Review low-expression DE instead of importing a forum cutoff
items.source_observation: In a scVI discussion, a user reports rare-gene DE calls; a reply contrasts the user's 30% detection filter with a personal 5% choice and another model-scale filter.
items.proposed_rule: Inspect observed counts, detection, donor consistency and effect estimates together. Predeclare any expression filter and investigate sensitivity rather than selecting a favorable result.
items.applicability_and_limits: These are scVI-specific experiences, not a validated universal 5% cutoff or a rule for PyDESeq2. Filtering only HVGs can also change which hypotheses are tested.
items.plugin_relationship: Our condition DE uses pseudobulk/PyDESeq2, so the forum thresholds must not be inserted directly.
items.review_question: How would you distinguish a rare but meaningful transcript from an unstable low-signal finding?
items.proposed_acceptance_check: Keep both unfiltered and explicitly filtered result tables and explain which conclusions depend on the filter.

items.title: Review a tutorial design formula against the sampling scheme
items.source_observation: The chapter describes eight patients in both conditions, constructs patient-condition pseudobulks, then shows a ~label model and motivates excluding patient terms using PCA patterns.
items.proposed_rule: Flag this example for statistical review before adoption. Specify paired or unpaired design from sampling metadata; PCA alone should not decide whether repeated observations are independent.
items.applicability_and_limits: This is our methodological concern about the displayed example, not a reproduction of its results or a claim that every conclusion in the chapter is wrong.
items.plugin_relationship: Our paired path uses ~donor+condition; this note does not alter it. Designs beyond the runner's formulas require a separate implementation.
items.review_question: Do you agree that the example needs an explicit paired-design discussion? Which comparison should we reproduce?
items.proposed_acceptance_check: On a suitable paired example, compare estimable design matrices and effect uncertainty with and without donor terms, with statistical review of the contrast.

items.title: Treat historical memory workarounds as version-specific
items.source_observation: A 2020 issue reports a backed-mode log1p/copy error with explicit old Scanpy and AnnData versions.
items.proposed_rule: Before applying a workaround, reproduce a minimal case in the installed environment and estimate memory cost. Preserve the original file and capture the actual traceback.
items.applicability_and_limits: The old report does not establish a current bug or imply that loading everything into memory is safe.
items.plugin_relationship: The current runner is not an out-of-core pipeline. A large-data execution path would need its own resource controls and tests.
items.review_question: What memory ceiling and fallback behavior would be acceptable on your workstation?
items.proposed_acceptance_check: An oversized job should provide a resource explanation rather than blindly densifying or replacing the source file.

items.title: Choose an enrichment background that matches gene eligibility
items.source_observation: GO guidance allows a reference/background list and explains that enrichment compares the submitted list against that reference.
items.proposed_rule: Define eligible genes, mapping losses, selection criteria, database release and multiple-testing scope before interpretation. Inspect the genes driving each term.
items.applicability_and_limits: An enrichment result is not itself a functional activity measurement or causal experiment. Ranked-list methods require their own contracts.
items.plugin_relationship: Enrichment remains a future extension; no GO/KEGG/Reactome analysis tool was added in this collection.
items.review_question: For your biological question, which genes could genuinely have entered the selected list?
items.proposed_acceptance_check: Compare justified background choices and flag terms whose interpretation changes; do not silently default to the whole genome.

items.title: Distinguish global gene filtering from test-specific filtering
items.source_observation: The Scanpy introduction uses a three-cell gene filter; the QC chapter later uses twenty cells; the DE chapter applies additional pseudobulk expression filters.
items.proposed_rule: Record the stage, unit and purpose of every filter. Review whether a global filter removes genes needed for a rare population before applying a downstream test-specific filter.
items.applicability_and_limits: These example thresholds are not interchangeable recommendations. A rare-cell marker can be lost under a global rule even when useful within its population.
items.plugin_relationship: Current QC defaults to detection in three retained cells; DE applies a separate aggregated-count filter. Changes require a reviewed case and implementation test.
items.review_question: Which rare populations or targeted genes should we explicitly monitor when assessing gene-filter sensitivity?
items.proposed_acceptance_check: Compare retained targeted genes and rare-population evidence under justified settings; preserve each tested gene universe in the report.
